rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address encompasses all people but especially targets the polytheists, the surah’s main audience; it follows 7:10, anticipates the address to Adam’s children in 7:27, and confronts polytheists’ excuses in 7:28.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للناس كلهم ، والمقصود منه المشركون ، لأنهم الغرض في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām and qad reinforce the report in the same way as the preceding verse’s wording.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر باللام و ( قد ) للوجه الذي تقدم في قوله : { ولقد خلقناكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural addressees are humanity as a kind, while creation and fashioning refer to their first ancestor Adam, as the following command concerning Adam clarifies.
rows.anchor: تعدية فعلي الخلق والتصوير إلى ضمير المخاطبين ، لما كان على معنى خلق النوع الذي هم من أفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means bringing something into existence; fashioning means giving it a form, the shape made for a body as clay is shaped.
rows.anchor: والتصوير جعل الشيء صورة ، والصورة الشكل الذي يشكل به الجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the higher rank of imaging as a perfection of creation: human form includes refined perception and deliberation, whether formed with Adam’s creation or later through embryonic development, as 23:14 describes.
rows.anchor: وعطفت جملة { صورناكم } بحرف ( ثم ) الدالة على تراخي رتبة التصوير عن رتبة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and fashioning address Adam, the first of humanity; treating creation of the species’ origin as creation of its descendants reminds them to thank their creator, as in 69:11.
rows.anchor: مراد منه أصل نوعهم الأول وهو آدم بقرينة تعقيبه بقوله : ثم قلنا للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows the verbs to mean that God intended to create and fashion them, comparing the prospective wording in the angels’ statement before Lot was ordered to leave.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يؤول فعلا الخلق والتصوير بمعنى إرادة حصول ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following command identifies Adam as the one created and fashioned: he emerged as a particular being named Adam, after which God displayed his excellence by commanding the angels to bow.
rows.anchor: خلقنا أصلكم وصورناه فبرز موجودا معينا مسمى بآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compressed transition from creating Adam to naming him and displaying his excellence through the prostration command is a strikingly concise construction.
rows.anchor: فوقع إيجاز بديع في نسج الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here thumma connects two clauses and marks rank, not elapsed time, because the prostration command is loftier in rank than the preceding creation clause.
rows.anchor: عاطفة الجملة على الجملة فهي مقيدة للتراخي الرتبي لا للتراخي الزماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural can denote the class without requiring every angel to be addressed; Ibn Abbas reports that the angels present where Adam was created may have been meant, while all angels are also possible.
rows.anchor: وتعريف الملائكة } للجنس فلا يلزم أن يكون الأمر عاما لجميع الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish that Adam was created in the angels’ realm: God may instead have gathered angels to show them the wondrous creation, since angels move between places.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أمر الله الملائكة بالسجود لآدم لا يقتضي أن يكون آدم قد خلق في العالم الذي فيه الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse’s apparent sense suggests Adam was created in heaven or in Paradise, the majority of Ahl al-Sunna adopt that apparent sense; Ibn Ashur says the verse is not decisive on the matter.
rows.anchor: وإن كان ظاهرها يقتضي ذلك ، وبهذا الظاهر أخذ جمهور أهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception indicates that Iblis was counted among the angels because he was mixed with them; al-Sakkaki explains this as inclusion by predominance.
rows.anchor: واستثناء إبليس من الساجدين في قوله : { إلا إبليس } يدل على أنه كان في عداد الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a circumstantial clause about Iblis and reinforces the exception, since the exception already entails that he did not share the angels’ action.
rows.anchor: وهي حال مؤكدة لمضمون عاملها وهو ما دلت عليه أداة الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying he was not one of the prostrators gives stronger force to the denial than merely saying he did not prostrate, as in the wording of 6:56.
rows.anchor: وفي اختيار الاخبار عن نفي سجوده بجعله من غير الساجدين : إشارة إلى أنه انتفى عنه السجود انتفاء شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis had a disposition toward disobedience whenever a command opposed his desire, unlike the angels; the latent disposition emerged when he was ordered to bow.
rows.anchor: ففي الآية إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى خلق في نفس إبليس جبلة تدفعه إلى العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies that Iblis was never destined to join the prostrators, with no expectation that he would later bow; this prepares for the ensuing interrogation.
rows.anchor: أي انتفى سجوده انتفاء لارجاء في حصوله بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The change from ‘We said’ to ‘He said’ is an iltifāt: God is understood as speaker, while the discourse shifts from addressing the angels to rebuking Iblis alone.
rows.anchor: وكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال : قلنا ، فكان العدول إلى ضمير الغائب التفاتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is genuinely a question but is tinged with reproach, and its purpose is to expose Iblis’s motive to the angels.
rows.anchor: و { ما } للاستفهام ، وهو استفهام ظاهره حقيقي ، ومشوب بتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected construction would be ‘what prevented you from prostrating’; the added lā is unexpected because Iblis was prevented from bowing, not from not bowing.
rows.anchor: فكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال : ما منعك أن تسجد لأنه إنما كف عن السجود لا عن نفي السجود

rows.speaker: الكسائي، والفراء، والزجاج، والزمخشري
rows.claim: They take lā as an emphatic extra particle with no negative force, comparing emphatic constructions in 90:1, 57:29, and 21:95.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل الكسائي ، والفراء ، والزجاج ، والزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects the emphatic-extra reading because emphasis normally confirms that an action occurred, whereas Iblis’s prostration did not occur.
rows.anchor: فلا ينبغي التعويل على هذا التأويل

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki reads lā as negative and understands an implied opposite action: preventing someone from bowing prompts him not to bow; thus manaʿaka is metaphorically ‘prompted you.’
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل السكاكي في ( المفتاح ) في فصل المجاز اللغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers the metaphorical ‘prompted you’ interpretation, also attributed to Abd al-Jabbar by al-Fakhr, a better explanation than treating lā as an emphatic extra.
rows.anchor: وقريب منه لعبد الجبار فيما نقله الفخر عنه ، وهو أحسن تأويلا

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari instead explains the construction as ellipsis: two verbs are intended, one stated and the other omitted but indicated by its complement.
rows.anchor: وأما أن يكون قد أريد الفعلان ، فذكر أحدهما وحذف الآخر ، وأشير إلى المحذوف بمتعلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refers readers to his discussion of the parallel question to Aaron in 20:92–93.
rows.anchor: وانظر ما قلته عند قوله تعالى : { قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا أن لا تتبعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase modifies ‘prostrate’; its attachment to God’s command means the command to the angels included Iblis.
rows.anchor: وتعليق ضميره بالأمر يقتضي أن أمر الملائكة شامل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes Iblis a class of angels, created as the progenitor of jinn with a capacity for sin; this is the Quran’s apparent sense and the view of many jurists, citing 18:50.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو ظاهر القرآن ، وإليه ذهب كثير من الفقهاء

rows.speaker: المعتزلة وبعض الأشاعرة
rows.claim: Another view treats jinn as a distinct immaterial kind and Iblis as their progenitor, included among the angels for the command; Muslim’s report from Aisha says angels were created from light and jinn from fire. Ibn Ashur allows fire as light mixed with matter and angelic light as immaterial.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب المعتزله وبعض الأشاعرة ، وقد يكون المراد من النار نورا مخلوطا بالمادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is set as dialogue; Iblis identifies his perceived superiority as the reason for refusing God’s command, making the refusal an explicit sin.
rows.anchor: وهذا معصية صريحة ، وقوله : { أنا خير منه } مسوق مساق التعليل للامتناع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘You created me from fire’ explains and clarifies Iblis’s claim that he is better than Adam.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { خلقتني من نار } بيان لجملة : { أنا خير منه } فلذلك فصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis could have learned his origin from angels who witnessed his creation or from God; 55:14–15 confirms that jinn were made from fire, and 18:50 identifies Iblis as a jinn.
rows.anchor: وحصل لإبليس العلم بكونه مخلوقا من نار ، بإخبار من الملائكة الذين شهدوا خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis grounds his self-ranking in the supposed superiority of his material element, fire, over Adam’s element, earth.
rows.anchor: واستند في تفضيل نفسه إلى فضيلة العنصر الذي خلق منه على العنصر الذي خلق منه آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire seems superior to soil through its force, dominance, light, and purity; both nevertheless contribute to living bodies. Angelic light is purer than fire’s material rays, while clay is earth mixed with life-supporting water.
rows.anchor: والنار أفضل من التراب لقوة تأثيرها وتسلطها على الأجسام التي تلاقيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew Adam deserved the command through a capacity for angelic purity; raw elemental nobility alone does not determine merit, since the creator’s arrangement and the capacities it produces matter.
rows.anchor: فأما إبليس فغره زكاء عنصره وذلك ليس كافيا في التفضيل وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s fiery constitution drives destructive, impulsive action, whereas Adam’s earthy constitution supports good and chosen growth; angels’ luminous constitution inclines them by nature to pure good without deliberation.
rows.anchor: وركب آدم من عنصر التراب على هيئة تجعله يستخدم آثار القوة العنصرية في الخبر والصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human ascent to angelic virtues is especially remarkable and descent to satanic vice especially easy; this is why humans are addressed with moral obligations.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كان بلوغ الإنسان إلى الفضائل الملكية أعلى وأعجب ، وكان مبلغه إلى الرذائل الشيطانية أحط وأسهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw before Adam’s address coordinates it within the quoted speech that began with the order to expel Iblis, rather than with the narrator’s preceding speech verb.
rows.anchor: الواو من قوله : { ويا آدم } عاطفة على جملة : { أخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speaker may turn from one addressee to another in the same setting without repeating ‘We said’; this arrangement heightens the humiliation of expelled Iblis as Adam receives favor before him.
rows.anchor: وفي توجيه الخطاب لآدم بهذه الفضيلة بحضور إبليس بعد طرده زيادة إهانة

rows.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: He cites the Prophet’s judgment in the case of a man and an Ansari: the sheep and servant woman were returned, the son received one hundred lashes and a year’s exile, and Unays was sent to investigate the wife’s confession.
rows.anchor: قول النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم في قضية الرجل والأنصاري الذي كان ابن الرجل عسيفا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Adam was already created in Paradise, ‘dwell’ means remain there; if he was created elsewhere, it grants him entry as an honor. Either reading taunts Iblis, who had scorned Adam.
rows.anchor: فالأمر في قوله : { اسكن } إنما هو أمر تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene’s placement gives the wording an additional meaning beyond its parallel in al-Baqara: it shows Adam honored in the setting where Iblis is being punished and expelled.
rows.anchor: فقد دل موقع هذا الكلام ، في هذه السورة ، على معنى عظيم من قمع إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrangement exemplifies a speaker addressing multiple people in one gathering, as in the ruler’s separate instructions to Joseph and his wife in 12:28–29.
rows.anchor: ومن أسلوب هذه الآية ما في قوله تعالى : { قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم يوسف أعرض عن هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The A‘raf address is directed to polytheists who made Satan their patron, while the parallel in al-Baqara admonishes Israelites who are wary of Satan.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الكلام مسوق إلى المشركين الذين اتخذوا الشيطان وليا من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative calls attention to Adam and honors him before the gathered company.
rows.anchor: والنداء للإقبال على آدم والتنويه بذكره في ذلك الملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit detached pronoun after the imperative further humiliates Iblis by implying that Adam is unlike him; context allows this indirect contrast even though pronouns have no inherent contrastive force.
rows.anchor: والإتيان بالضمير المنفصل بعد الأمر ، لقصد زيادة التنكيل بإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa here, unlike the wāw in 2:35, makes permission to eat follow immediately on the order to dwell, signaling prompt and complete favor that intensifies Iblis’s distress.
rows.anchor: فالآية هنا أفادت أن الله تعالى أذن آدم بأن يتمتع بثمار الجنة عقب أمره بسكنى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Baqara the focus is reminding Israelites of Adam’s favor, sin, and repentance and warning them against Satan’s guile, so the audience and narrative purpose differ.
rows.anchor: وأما آية البقرة فإنما أفادت السامعين أن الله امتن على آدم بمنة سكنى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that the subtle implication of the detached pronoun in this address also applies to al-Baqara, though he had previously missed it there.
rows.anchor: وهذه نكتة فاتني العلم بها في آية سورة البقرة فضمها إليها أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Baqara account also honors Adam with the word ‘abundantly’ (raghadan); together the two accounts distribute several favors across the story.
rows.anchor: على أن آية البقرة ( 35 ) لم تخل عن ذكر ما فيه تكرمة له وهو قوله : رغدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banning even approach to the tree warns more strongly than banning its fruit, by blocking the means that could lead to eating it.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة } أشد في التحذير من أن ينهى عن الأكل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition was probably a test: one tree was excluded amid permitted trees to train resistance to appetite and gradually establish humanity’s cognitive faculties through its first ancestor.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الظاهر ليتكون مختلف القوى العقلية في عقل النوع بتأسيسها في أصل النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account, Adam’s first impulse to disobey and eating from the tree brought an instinctive awareness of shortcomings and ended his simple, naive state.
rows.anchor: فأعقبه الأكل حدوث خاطر الشعور بما فيه من نقايص أدركها بالفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the tree’s nature awakened knowledge of good and evil, as in the Torah’s account of the tree of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك لخصوصية في طبع تلك الشجرة أن تثير في النفس علم الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur regards the intrinsic knowledge-tree explanation as unlikely; he reads the story as depicting human cognition’s development, like Adam’s learning the names in 2:31.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندي بعيد ، وإنما حكى الله لنا هيئة تطور العقل البشري في خلقة أصل النوع البشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree is presented as visible, but reports identifying its species are weak; he refers that discussion to al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى شجرة مشاهدة وقد رويت روايات ضعيفة في تعيين نوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an distributes Adam’s favors among accounts to renew listeners’ interest, vary the narration, and serve its main goals of moral instruction and example.
rows.anchor: ليحصل تجديد الفائدة ، تنشيطا للسامع ، وتفننا في أساليب الحكاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjunctive after the prohibition presents becoming wrongdoers as a consequence of approaching the forbidden tree, not as a consequence of the act of prohibition itself.
rows.anchor: وانتصب : { فتكونا } على جواب النهي ، والكون من الظالمين متسبب على القرب المنهي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subjunctive response tracks causation from the forbidden action; a jussive response instead treats the result as an answer to the prohibition’s speech act, by analogy with a condition.
rows.anchor: أن يعتبر التسبب على الفعل المنفي أو المنهي ، بخلاف الجزم في جواب النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘wrongdoers’ are those who deserve that description either by harming themselves through bad consequences or by violating God’s right to obedience.
rows.anchor: إما لظلمهم أنفسهم وإلقائها في العواقب السيئة ، وإما لاعتدائهم على حق غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa marks the whispering as close in time to Adam’s prohibition from eating; the interval is understood relative to the action.
rows.anchor: كانت وسوسة الشيطان بقرب نهي آدم عن الأكل من الشجرة ، فعبر عن القرب بحرف التعقيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is discreet speech audible only to someone nearby; the poet Ru’ba’s line supplies an Arab usage example for the term.
rows.anchor: والوسوسة الكلام الخفي الذي لا يسمعه إلا المداني للمتكلم ، قال رؤبة يصف صائدا

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ru’ba uses waswasa for the hunter’s quiet invocation of the Lord of daybreak, witnessing the word’s sense of covert speech.
rows.anchor: وسوس يدعو جاهدا رب الفلق سرا وقد أون تأوين العقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil’s waswasa was a covert, manipulative suggestion, delivered either in hushed words or as an inward impulse, like a deceiver hiding his scheme from bystanders.
rows.anchor: وسمي إلقاء الشيطان وسوسة : لأنه ألقى إليهما تسويلا خفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account elsewhere expresses this suggestion as spoken words to Adam (20:120), while Quranic usage also names harmful inner promptings waswasa (114:4).
rows.anchor: وقد وقع في الآية الأخرى التعبير عن تسويل الشيطان بالقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This detailed depiction of Satan’s scheme is distinctive to al-A‘raf, fitting its address to polytheists who lack this knowledge and need the devil’s deeds made vivid.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفصيل لإلقاء الشيطان كيده انفردت به هذه الآية عن آية سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may mark an unintended consequence if Satan did not know disobedience would produce awareness of evil and exposure of their private parts; this resembles the outcome in 28:8.
rows.anchor: واللام في : { ليبدي } لام العاقبة إذا كان الشيطان لا يعلم أن العصيان يفضي بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose: Satan may have known the outcome by inspiration, inference, or earlier knowledge, and aimed to make them disobey and suffer harm.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون لام العلة الباعثة إذا كان الشيطان يعلم ذلك بالإلهام أو بالنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either way, Satan intended harm because enmity toward humanity was settled in his nature, as stated explicitly in 35:6.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد استقر في طبعه عداوة البشر ، كما سيصرح به فيما بعد
